title: Frequency Response of the CS Stage
intro: The CS stage has two nodes with capacitance, giving two poles, plus a zero from the bridging capacitor CGD.

blocks.source:
Input pole:  1/[ RS * ( CGS + (1 + gm*RD)*CGD ) ]
Output pole: 1/[ RD * ( CL + CGD ) ]
Zero (RHP):  s = gm / CGD

blocks.text: The zero at gm/CGD is in the right half plane; it adds phase lag rather than lead and is usually well above the poles, but it matters in high-speed designs. The input pole is usually dominant when RS is large because of the Miller multiplication. In that case the bandwidth is set by RS and the Miller capacitance.

Increase RS: the dominant input pole drops quickly and the Miller curve parts from the 'no Miller' curve, which shows how much bandwidth the multiplication costs. Reduce RS to make the output pole dominant instead.

blocks.title: Poles of a stage
blocks.text: gm = 2 mS, RD = 10 kohm, RS = 10 kohm, CGS = 100 fF, CGD = 30 fF, CL = 200 fF. Find the two poles.
solution: The input pole is dominant; the bandwidth is about 22 MHz.
